title: Emergency scenarios
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y11 lesson 5 (Emergency scenarios (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 5: Choking and severe bleeding. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Mild or severe choking?
points: Severe: cannot cough, speak or breathe

model.title: A deep cut to the forearm is bleeding heavily.

parts.text: Check danger; call 999 (or ask someone to)
Press firmly with a clean cloth
Keep pressing; add pads, do not lift to look
Watch for shock: pale, cold, fast breathing

questions.q: Your uncle is coughing hard after swallowing a fish bone; he can speak.
questions.a: Mild choking: encourage him to keep coughing; do not give back blows yet.

questions.q: A woman at a picnic clutches her throat; she cannot speak, cough or breathe.
questions.a: Severe choking: up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts; repeat; call 999 if not cleared; CPR if she becomes unresponsive.

questions.q: A man has cut his forearm deeply on glass and it is bleeding heavily.
questions.a: Call 999; press firmly on the wound with a clean pad; keep pressure and add pads on top; do not remove anything stuck in it; watch for shock.

questions.q: An adult collapses, does not respond and is not breathing normally.
questions.a: Call 999 on speaker, send for an AED, start CPR (30 compressions, 2 breaths if trained or hands-only), use the AED.

keywords.def: firm blows between the shoulder blades to clear a blockage
sharp inward and upward pulls above the navel
pressing firmly on a wound to slow bleeding

questions.q: Order: abdominal thrusts, encourage cough, back blows, call 999.
questions.a: Encourage cough, back blows, abdominal thrusts, call 999.

questions.q: Core: Emergency scenarios (pupil PDF): choose the right first aid for four situations.
questions.a: Correct actions for choking and bleeding scenarios.

questions.q: Extend: Check your home first aid kit with a parent and list what is missing.
Stretch: In the portal response box, explain why you should not remove an object stuck in a wound.
questions.a: It may be plugging the wound; removing it can cause heavy bleeding.

questions.q: A choking adult can still cough strongly. What should you do?
questions.a: B) Encourage them to keep coughing. A strong cough is the best way to clear a mild blockage.

questions.q: Severe choking: first action? A) give water B) up to 5 back blows C) wait
Big question: someone at the table cannot speak or cough. What do you do?
questions.a: Back blows, then abdominal thrusts, call 999 if not cleared.
